key_messages: Widespread moderate, but beneficial, rainfall will fall across the region Tuesday and Tuesday night as a frontal boundary stalls over the region.
Periods of breezy winds are expected through early Thursday.

A strong low pressure system will pass through the St. Lawrence Valley and will bring widespread rainfall and even some mountain snow Friday into Saturday with sharply cooler temperatures into the weekend.
Gusty winds will accompany the late week system Friday into Saturday, slowly relaxing by Saturday night.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
323 PM EDT Mon Oct 12 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 252 PM EDT Monday...

Precipitation amounts were increased by around 50% across
northern Vermont and the Adirondacks for Tuesday and Tuesday
night. The potential for gusty winds is continued to be watched
closely Friday into Saturday. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 252 PM EDT Monday...

1. Widespread moderate, but beneficial, rainfall will fall
across the region Tuesday and Tuesday night as a frontal
boundary stalls over the region. 

2. Periods of breezy winds are expected through early Thursday. 

3. A strong low pressure system will pass through the St. 
Lawrence Valley and will bring widespread rainfall and even some 
mountain snow Friday into Saturday with sharply cooler temperatures 
into the weekend. 

4. Gusty winds will accompany the late week system Friday into 
Saturday, slowly relaxing by Saturday night.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 252 PM EDT Monday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: A cold front will be dropping southward this
evening with rain chances increasing overnight as the parent low
ejects into the northern Atlantic off eastern Canada. The result
will be for the boundary to stall out over the region for
Tuesday through Tuesday night as another fast moving clipper
style system approaches from the west. This wave will increase 
southerly flow across the quasi-stationary boundary deepening 
moisture advection and increasing isentropic lift across the 
boundary. This will result in an extended period of wet 
conditions for the Adirondacks and north/central Vermont.
Initial rainfall will favor upslope areas of the Adirondacks 
and the northern Greens with westerly flow aloft. However, 
overnight into Tuesday, flow turns more southerly and deepens 
promoting strong moisture advection across the stalled boundary.
This flow direction will result in increased precipitation 
amounts with a lack of shadowing. As such, precipitation amounts
were increased area wide, with lowest totals around 0.5" 
towards southern Vermont to 1-2 inches tonight through Tuesday 
night from central Vermont northward. Highest amounts will be 
over the northern Greens and Adirondacks, but 1-1.75" is 
possible even for lower elevations in northern Vermont and 
northern New York. A few thunderstorms will be possible, 
especially Tuesday morning with a trough sweeping through and 
again Tuesday afternoon with the low approaching. This setup may
promote some cold air damming east of the Greens, with highs 
Tuesday below 50 degrees in northeastern Vermont. 

KEY MESSAGE 2: As the boundary drops southward this evening
winds in the northern Champlain Valley will briefly increase
with northerly winds of 15 to 25 mph and some gusts to around 30
mph across Lake Champlain. These winds will drop after midnight.
Next, a low level jet that will amplify the moisture across the
stationary boundary will move through Tuesday increasing
southerly flow mainly for the northern Champlain Valley since
moisture will dampen wind potential. Mixing over the lake may be
sufficient to intermittently bring some of these moderate gusts
to around 30 mph down to the lake surface. Finally, a stronger
push Wednesday will shunt the stationary boundary southward with
northerly breezes developing behind a reinforcing boundary.
Gusts 20 to 35 mph will be possible with stronger ridge level
winds expected. 

KEY MESSAGE 3: A northern stream Alberta clipper will phase with a 
southern stream closed low leading to an amplifying strong shortwave 
by early Friday. Widespread rain is expected Friday before 
temperatures sharply cool Friday night with the potential to see a 
switch to terrain snow showers Friday night into Saturday. Widespread 
rainfall amounts above half an inch are likely with 80-100% ensemble 
probabilities of 0.5 inches or more on Friday before any 
precipitation transitions to a rain snow mix in the terrain. Trends 
continue to denote likely probabilities of an inch or more with 60-
90% chances across the Adirondacks, and much of central and northern 
Vermont as well. Consensus favors our northern zones as the focus of 
the highest precipitation amounts with this system. 

A cold front will sweep through the area Friday night sharply 
lowering temperatures 10 to 15 degrees from Friday evening to 
Saturday morning. Temperatures will likely dip below freezing for 
most if not all locations across the area with only those near Lake 
Champlain and immediately near the St. Lawrence River staying above 
freezing. As temperatures fall, snow levels during the day Saturday 
will also lower to 500-1000ft agl, with a transition to snow above 
1500ft agl, and a rain, wet snow mix, in elevations between 1000-
1500ft agl. A few mixed in flurries cannot be ruled our even in the 
Champlain Valley, though temperatures will be marginal in the mid to 
upper 30s. Some snowliage appears likely with ensembles denoting 
nearly 100% chances for purely snowfall in the Adirondacks and 
Northeast Kingdom. Snowfall impacts will be minimal with road 
temperatures well above freezing, and with only marginal surface 
temperatures, snow will likely be of a wet character, with minor 
accumulation only on the highest elevations and mainly on vegetation 
only. Most locations will not see any accumulations at this point. 

Rain and snow showers will taper off Saturday evening as the system 
pulls away to the northeast. 850 mb temperatures Saturday night will 
be remarkably cold for this time of year in the -9 to -11C range 
Saturday night supporting temperatures in the 20s for most of the 
area, including the entire Champlain Valley. Pockets of teens will 
be possible in the coldest hollows of the Adirondacks and Northeast 
Kingdom as surface temperatures anomalies will be 10 degrees below 
normal. Temperatures will slowly moderate back towards seasonable 
normals to start next week.

KEY MESSAGE 4: The dynamic end of week system will deepen as it
approaches the St. Lawrence Valley Friday with a strengthening 
pressure and thermal gradient. While there are slight 
differences to the overall track of the center of the system, 
strong gusty south winds are expected Friday, followed by strong
cold advective northwesterly winds by Saturday. The GFS favors 
a more northward low center track which would enhance the 
southerly flow Friday after in the Champlain and the St. 
Lawrence Valley, whereas the Euro favors a low center directly 
over the Champlain Valley Friday with slight weaker southerly 
flow. Regardless of track, gusts Friday are favored to be 
upwards of 35 MPH for the Champlain Valley, with a 50-70% chance
for high end values up to 40 MPH in the ensemblistic guidance. 
Slightly weaker winds to 20-30 MPH elsewhere Friday. Winds will 
turn to the northwest Friday night with better confidence in 
stronger winds Saturday due to a lack of precipitation 
limitations that exist Friday. Sustained winds will increase to 
20 to 25 MPH, with 55-80% chance for gusts over 40 MPH from the 
Adirondacks eastward on Saturday. Recreators should also plan 
for mountain summit gusts as high as 40-55 MPH, especially in 
the Adirondacks. Surface winds will slowly weaken back towards 
10 MPH or less Saturday night with gusts and mountain winds 
following suit by Sunday.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z MONDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Through 18Z Tuesday...A complex TAF forecast is expected through
the next 24 hours for all terminals. A dynamic weather system 
will approach the region this evening into tomorrow with 
deteriorating conditions overnight tonight. Widespread variable 
cigs from IFR to high MVFR will continue towards sunset before 
probabilities of IFR cigs increasing from 10-20% to around 
30-50% for many terminals between 22-24Z. Blocked flow will 
increase after 22Z, with low level moisture likely resulting in 
BKN006-BKN009 cigs for BTV/EFK/MPV/RUT. IFR cigs for the 
aforementioned locations is low to moderate, with expectations 
that there will be bouncing conditions for a while after sunset.
SLK is expected to remain IFR through the TAF period. Light 
showers and mist return this evening as well beyond 22Z with 
winds turning more northwesterly for all terminals, outside of 
MSS which will see northeast channeled flow, and increasing to 
around 10 knots for MSS/BTV/PBG. Variable cigs between high IFR 
and low MVFR is expected for all terminals between 00-07Z. 
Confidence in IFR cigs beyond 07Z for all terminals will be high
beyond 07Z as a sharp inversion develops across the area with 
ongoing light showers and mist. Blocked flow will also 
strengthen resulting in IFR cig probabilities even at BTV 
between 50-60% beyond 07Z. 

The most impactful portion of this period will be after daybreak 
tomorrow when light to moderate rain will move from west to east. 
Visibilities will lower towards 2 to 4SM after 10Z with slight cig 
improvements to 1000-1500ft agl, outside of SLK which will remain 
IFR. LLWS will develop at mountain terminals with a strong low level 
jet to 40 knots at 2000ft agl. Winds concurrently will increase to 
10 to 15 knots with gusts as high as 25 knots by 18Z tomorrow from 
the southwest, especially at BTV/MPV. MSS will see continued 
channeled flow from the northeast through the TAF period.

Outlook...

Tuesday Night: MVFR/IFR conditions possible. Definite SHRA,
Slight chance TSRA.
Wednesday: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Slight chance
SHRA.
Wednesday Night: Mainly MVFR, with areas VFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Thursday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Thursday Night: VFR. Chance SHRA.
Friday: Mainly MVFR, with areas IFR possible. Definite SHRA.
Friday Night: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Windy with
gusts to 30 kt. Chance SHRA.
Saturday: Mainly MVFR, with areas VFR possible. Windy with gusts
to 30 kt. Slight chance SHRA, Slight chance SHSN.

&&

.MARINE...
Periods of rough lake conditions are anticipated this week into
the weekend. This evening, a brief period of breezy conditions 
are anticipated as flow turns out of the north. Flow flips
Tuesday with a low level jet moving across the region with
southerly breezes developing and potential resulting in periods
of rough lake conditions. Additional periods of concern will be
later Wednesday and again Friday into Saturday as a couple of
fronts move through the region. Overall, it will not be a 
pleasant week to venture out on Lake Champlain, especially in
smaller watercraft. 


&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&
